proof_summary: Any hypothetical witness below $2^{2^k+1}$ must have totient exactly $2^{2^k}$ and be odd, hence is a squarefree product of distinct Fermat primes; comparing totients gives a sum of distinct powers of two equal to $2^k$, forcing the $k$-th Fermat number to be prime and to divide the witness. This excludes smaller witnesses in either primality case, while the $k$-th Fermat number itself (when prime) or $2^{2^k+1}$ supplies the matching upper bound.
